meta.title: Generic 2 MOA tube red-dot sight: optical system, zero tables and rendering model
meta.units: millimetres, degrees, MOA or mrad as each key says; SI in the zero tables; sockets in metres
meta.class_references: External figures of the class come from the Aimpoint CompM4 user manual, section 1.1 (135 x 51 x 57 mm, 370 g, 2 MOA, 16 positions, unlimited eye relief, 1 click = 16 mm at 100 m, +/- 2 m at 100 m). This is a generic sight: no maker's name, logo or trade dress; the optical prescription is solved here.

frames.asset: metres, +Z muzzle, +Y up, +X shooter's left; origin socket_mount = the rifle's socket_optic (rail top, on the centreline)
frames.shooter: eye offsets and angles as the shooter sees them: right and up; right = -X of the asset frame
frames.lens: the collimator's frame: ex sagittal, ey tangential (+ey points away from the emitter)
frames.centred_eye_beam_note: direction of the dot for the centred eye relative to the mechanical axis (rad, lens frame); zeroing absorbs it, and every other angle here is relative to it

design.type: off-axis Mangin doublet collimator: LED at the tube wall, dichroic on the cemented surface
design.window_deviation_note: the tilted meniscus window bends the line of sight by this constant angle (a weak wedge); zeroing absorbs it, and the parallax figures are measured from the point the centred eye's dot covers through the window
design.note: R1, R2 and the emitter focus position are solved here by minimising the parallax error over a 14 mm eye disc at 50 m; the tilt puts the centred eye's dot on the mechanical axis; R3 makes the window afocal.

parallax.definition: angle between the dot and the target point the centred eye aimed at, as the eye moves off the optical axis; POI moves opposite: poi_shift = -error * distance
parallax.frame: lens frame: ex = sagittal, ey = tangential (+ey is away from the LED). See frames.lens_from_shooter for the shooter's right/up

beam_direction_poly.doc: a_x, a_y (rad) = sum c[i][j] * ex^i * ey^j, eye offsets in mm; error(e, D) = a(e) + k * e / (D * 1000 + eye_plane_behind_window_mm) per axis, D = target distance from the front window (m), k = see_through_factor (1 for a perfect 1x window)

parallax.sweep_note: edge_to_edge_sweep_moa: the eye goes from -11 to +11 mm across the window; the figure is how far the dot moves on the target

window.look: seen through: a faint cyan-blue cast (red is taken out of the scene); seen from the front: a deep red mirror-like flash
window.rear_window: plain AR-coated flat, 0.5 percent per surface, neutral
window.eye_side_ghost: the eye-side surface of the doublet reflects about 0.5 percent of what is behind the shooter (bright sky behind gives a faint veil)
window.source: inferred: reflectance and bandwidth typical of a single-line band reflector; the tint is computed from that spectrum with the Wyman 2013 fit of the CIE 1931 observer under a 6504 K source

appearance.bloom_model: apparent diameter = dot * sqrt(1 + (C / 300)); add a halo of radius 6 * dot at 0.02 * C / 300 of the core (clamped to 1), plus two faint starburst spikes for C > 1000
appearance.astigmatism_note: a real eye with astigmatism smears the dot into a comma; not modelled, expose as an option

brightness.source: inferred: step ratio 3 per daylight position and a 2e5 cd/m^2 top setting chosen so the top position keeps contrast above 6 on sunlit snow; manufacturers publish the number of settings, not luminances

turrets.elevation: top, coin-slot adjuster under a screw cap; clip elevation_adjust
turrets.windage: right side, the same; clip windage_adjust
turrets.mechanism: the adjusters move the emitter: 13.9 um per click

eye_relief: unlimited (a collimated dot). The design eye point 159 mm behind the rear window only fixes the head position.

reticle.name: 2 MOA dot
reticle.profile: radial: uniform luminance to r = 0.291 mrad, then a Gaussian skirt of sigma 0.06 mrad (about the eye's point spread at a 3 mm pupil: inferred)

zero.convention: Distances are from the eye. bore_angle is the bore above the line of sight for an exact zero (POI = POA at the zero distance). clicks_up_from_centre is that angle in whole clicks from optical centre (line of sight parallel to the bore); the hold tables use the exact angle. poi_mm: + is high. hold: aim this much higher (+) to hit.

rendering.frame: Asset frame (metres, +Z muzzle, +Y up, +X shooter's left), origin socket_mount. The optical axis is the line through socket_eye and socket_objective.
steps: 1. Draw the world as usual. The housing, mount and caps are ordinary opaque geometry.
2. On pixels of the front window seen through the rear window (materials lens_front and lens_rear): multiply the scene by window.transmission_linear_srgb.

3. Dot direction: d = optical axis + zero offset + a(eye offset), with a from optics.parallax.beam_direction_poly rotated by frames.lens_from_shooter (OpticRedDot.dotDirection does this). The dot is at infinity: draw a disc of angular diameter dot.size_mrad around d. It has a fixed angular size and does not scale with how big the window is on screen.
4. The dot exists only on window pixels: when the line from the eye along d misses the front or rear clear aperture the dot is gone. That is the whole "eye box" of a red dot.
5. Dot radiance = led colour * brightness.settings[position].dot_luminance_cd_m2 / exposure. Bloom and wash-out follow brightness.appearance from the Weber contrast.

6. Optional: 0.5 percent environment reflection on the front surface tinted window.front_reflection_linear_srgb, a 0.5 percent ghost of the scene behind the shooter, and a dark ring in the outer 6 percent of the window radius (the tube wall seen through the edge of the doublet).
rendering.parallax_shortcut: error (rad) = e * (1/D - 1/D0) per lens axis, e = eye offset (m), D0 = optics.parallax.parallax_free_distance_m. The polynomial adds the aberration terms, which dominate beyond about 6 mm of eye offset.
rendering.source: led colour: inferred, a 650 nm LED in linear sRGB primaries (out of gamut, clipped)

parity_samples.doc: exact ray-trace values for optic-red-dot.js to reproduce: beam direction a (rad) and parallax error (rad, shooter right/up) per distance (m)

lens_trace.doc: the numbers the runtime needs for its own exact trace (lens frame, mm; window vertex at the origin, +z toward the target)
